content.user_title: Test Smart Contracts With Hardhat and Foundry
content.value_statement: Smart contract defects can be expensive and hard to reproduce. This skill guides structured Hardhat and Foundry tests, fork tests, fuzzing, gas checks, and coverage.
actual_capabilities: Set up Hardhat testing with forking, gas reporting, coverage, and verification plugins.
Write unit tests for ownership, balances, events, reverts, and time-based behavior.
Build Foundry tests with cheatcodes, fuzzing, account impersonation, and forked state.
Design mainnet fork tests against known DeFi contracts and token interfaces.
Compare gas usage between contract implementations.
Add coverage commands and CI workflow examples for automated test runs.
limitations: Does not provide complete production contract implementations.
Requires an existing Hardhat, Foundry, Node.js, and Solidity project setup.
Uses placeholder RPC endpoints, contract addresses, and secrets that users must configure safely.
Does not replace an independent smart contract security audit.

use_cases.title: Build Regression Test Suites
use_cases.description: Create repeatable unit tests for token contracts, access controls, events, reverts, and time-based logic.

use_cases.title: Validate Forked Market Behavior
use_cases.description: Test protocol interactions against fixed mainnet state before changing DeFi integrations or upgrade paths.

use_cases.title: Measure Coverage and Gas Risk
use_cases.description: Add coverage reporting, gas comparisons, and CI checks to improve release confidence.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Test Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for unit test coverage.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Hardhat test plan for my ERC-20 contract. Include ownership, transfers, events, reverts, and fixture setup.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Fork Testing
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for realistic integration tests.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a mainnet fork test for my DeFi integration. Use a fixed block number and list required mocked inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Add Foundry Fuzz Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Foundry fuzz tests for this Solidity function. Identify invariants, assumptions, edge cases, and expected revert paths.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Full Test Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my smart contract test strategy. Find gaps across unit tests, fork tests, fuzzing, gas checks, coverage, and CI automation.

output_examples.input: I need tests for an ERC-20 token with ownership and transfers.
output: A fixture-based test structure with owner and user accounts.
Assertions for supply assignment, balance changes, transfer events, and insufficient balance reverts.
A short list of edge cases for zero address and time-dependent behavior.

output_examples.input: I want to test a Uniswap integration on a forked chain.
output: A fork test plan using a fixed block number and configured RPC URL.
Setup steps for router and token interfaces.
Checks for swap behavior, balances, approvals, and revert conditions.

output_examples.input: Our release needs stronger test confidence.
output: A coverage and gas checklist for CI.
Recommended Foundry fuzz targets and invariants.
A list of missing negative tests and access-control cases.

best_practices: Use isolated fixtures and deterministic block numbers for repeatable results.
Keep test wallets, RPC URLs, and API keys in local secret storage.
Combine unit, fork, fuzz, coverage, and gas tests before release.
anti_patterns: Using live private keys or mainnet accounts in local test configs.
Depending only on happy-path transfer tests for DeFi logic.
Running fork tests without fixed block numbers.

faq.question: Does this skill work with both Hardhat and Foundry?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Hardhat JavaScript examples and Foundry Solidity test patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with mainnet fork tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains fixed-block fork setup and testing against existing mainnet contracts.

faq.question: Does it generate production deployment scripts?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on testing, coverage, gas checks, verification examples, and CI workflows.

faq.question: Should I use real private keys with these examples?
faq.answer: No. Use test-only keys and secure local secret storage for all RPC and API credentials.

faq.question: Can it replace a security audit?
faq.answer: No. It improves test quality, but smart contracts still need independent security review.

faq.question: What projects benefit most from this skill?
faq.answer: Solidity projects that need unit tests, DeFi fork tests, fuzzing, gas checks, coverage, and CI.
